pitch.the_claim: Slug your whole face with Vaseline every night for a month and here's what happens to your skin.
pitch.why_it_stitches: 1.13M in 1.7d (1.6M/day) with 458 comments — the fastest-rising in-lane video on the board and the civilian side of theme 3 (derm.talk's ♥-gold 'cheapest night cream' card, your zinc-oxide card). A 'what if' format from a non-derm science/explainer account, not a derm — punches sideways. Half-right: occlusion is real barrier repair for dry/compromised skin; nightly, all-over, for 30 days is wrong for oily/acne-prone skin and wrong over actives.
pitch.your_fit: Corpus: this is yours — 'If you're slugging with this much Vaseline, you're doing it wrong' (duet, TT, Sep 2023, 157K); 'a barrier cream can be as simple as Vaseline or Aquaphor' (skin-type test, Feb 2024); 'do not put Vaseline or any other occlusive moisturizer over active ingredients… it traps the moisture and the heat in' (rosacea tips, Jul 2023); 'if you have a damaged skin barrier, use zinc oxide cream' (Feb 2026) — and your zinc-oxide barrier card is 1.0d old (66K). Position stated; the 30-NIGHTS framing is the new angle (who it helps, who it breaks out).

'you want me to WHAT?' — slug over your retinol and you've built a sauna for your face

news.headline: 7 of 10 sunscreens miss their SPF label — Beauty of Joseon, Sun Bum among them; TGA now weighing action
news.summary: Consumer NZ's Oct 30 release (press-release dateline Friday 30 October 2026; 1News same day; CHOICE follow-up updated 30 Oct 2026): 7 of 10 sunscreens failed their SPF claims — Coola Zinc Oxide Lotion 50 tested SPF 14; Sun Bum Mineral 38, Beauty of Joseon Ginseng Sun Moist Serum 41, Invisible Zinc Sport 42, Le Tan 46, Natio 47, Marine Blue 34 (all labelled 50+); Cetaphil Sun met its claim. Story is day 4 but still rolling: SmartCompany (Nov 3) reports the TGA is 'considering the results' for regulatory action. Three US/TikTok-famous brands in one SPF scandal — no tracked creator is on it yet.
news.her_angle: 'your SPF 50 might be an SPF 14' — why the number on the tube isn't the number on your skin, and why the fix is MORE sunscreen, not a different tube
news.source: Consumer NZ release via Scoop (dateline Fri 30 Oct 2026) · 1News (Oct 30) · CHOICE (updated 30 Oct 2026) · SmartCompany follow-up (Nov 3, 2026)
